list.title: Wiki list
list.alt: Live Wiki list with category counts, visibility labels and one active tab style

items.shipped: Categories show how many pages each holds, and an Uncategorized bucket shows what still needs a tag.
items.gapBody: A fixed category list that almost nobody fills in: 18 pages, 3 of them categorized.

items.shipped: Each row shows who can see it with an icon and a name: a building for everyone, a team icon, a lock for private.
items.gapBody: "Private to buildingadmin@…" names an address, not who can actually see the page.

items.shipped: Tabs share one underline style. Unpublished and clearable counts sit on their own and stay visible on every tab.
items.gapBody: Two different "selected" styles. The orange Drafts tab looks active even when it isn't.

editor.title: Editor
editor.alt: Live editor with structured steps and a separate Published status

items.shipped: Steps carry time, Warning, Verify, Note and Key labels from my step editor. The Markdown body above them is still there.
items.gapBody: "Use ## for a heading" asks frontline staff to learn syntax before they can write.

items.shipped: Draft or Published sits under the visibility panel, apart from the settings authors edit.
items.gapBody: "Draft · Not yet saved" sits inside the editable settings card, where it reads like an option.

applies.title: Applies to
applies.alt: Live editor Applies to section with picked categories, asset types, tags, keywords, job roles and related wikis

items.shipped: Categories, asset types and asset tags are picked from the platform’s own lists, so spelling stays consistent for search and the AI.
items.gapBody: Categories, asset types and keywords are free text, so they stay empty and the agent has nothing to match on.

items.shipped: My addition beyond the audit: pages are tagged with the job roles that use them, one more signal for routing.
Also my addition: authors link pages a reader should see together, so one procedure leads to the next.

review.title: Review
review.alt: Live review page with struck-through replaced steps, a step comment and three decision buttons

items.shipped: Every changed step shows the old text struck through and the new text beside it. Reviewers comment on a step and choose Approve, Request changes or Reject.
items.gapBody: One Accept / Decline for the whole page, no inline comments, and only step 1 shows what changed.
